title: Runtime autotune framework: telemetry contracts and tuning playbook
author: Priya Nair
summary: Specification and operational playbook for the Runtime Autotune Framework: telemetry contracts, experiment design, safety controls, and oncall procedures for automated kernel and batching parameter tuning.
body:
Overview

This page documents the Runtime Autotune Framework (RAF): an orchestrated system that ingests workload telemetry, runs controlled optimization experiments, and produces validated parameter updates (kernel selection, batch sizing, concurrency caps, and quantization profiles) that can be rolled out to production runtime clusters. The goal of RAF is to improve per-token cost and tail latency while preserving correctness and customer-visible SLOs.

Goals and non-goals

- Goals:
  - Automate routine tuning for stable workloads to reduce manual effort and cost by 10–30% over time.
  - Maintain or improve 95/99/99.9 latency SLOs; never trade away SLOs for cost without an explicit human approval step.
  - Provide clear telemetry contracts so experiments are reproducible and auditable.
- Non-goals:
  - RAF does not perform model-level parameter changes (weights) or retrain models.
  - RAF is not intended to replace incident response; automated rollbacks exist for safety but oncall intervention is required for complex degradations.

High-level architecture

1) Telemetry ingestion: continuous metrics stream and structured trace events are ingested into the RAF experiment service.
2) Workload profiler: synthesizes request distributions (sequence length, prompt prefix similarity, token-per-request distribution, function-calls frequency).
3) Hypothesis generator: maps workload fingerprints to candidate tuning vectors (e.g., kernel A for short sequences, mixed-kernels for long tails).
4) Controlled experiment runner: executes traffic-shaping A/B/canary experiments in isolated slices.
5) Validator and safety checker: compares aggregated metrics against acceptance criteria and generates signed decisions.
6) Rollout manager: applies changes according to rollout policy (canary -> gradual -> global) with automatic rollback triggers.

Telemetry contract (required fields)

Every signal used by RAF must implement the following contract. Signals are exported as Prometheus metrics or annotated traces with the following stable names and labels. Table reflects canonical names used across customers and internal deployments.

- Metric namespace: redwood_runtime_autotune_* (Prometheus)

| Metric name | Type | Description | Required labels | Collection frequency | Notes |
|-------------|------|-------------|-----------------|----------------------|-------|
| redwood_runtime_autotune_request_seq_length | histogram | Request input token count distribution | model, region, shard | 1m | Buckets: 0-32,33-64,65-128,129-256,257-512,512+ |
| redwood_runtime_autotune_latency_seconds | summary | End-to-end request latency (s) including network + kernel exec | model, region, shard, priority | 10s | Quantiles: 0.5,0.95,0.99,0.999 |
| redwood_runtime_autotune_kernel_cpu_ms | counter | Cumulative CPU ms used by kernel selection per request | model, kernel_variant, shard | 1m | Reset on process restart |
| redwood_runtime_autotune_kvcache_hit_ratio | gauge | KV-cache prefix hit ratio (0..1) | model, shard | 30s | Critical for batching decisions |
| redwood_runtime_autotune_error_counts | counter | Categorized error counts (parse, model-mismatch, oom, timeout) | model, error_type, region | 10s | Must increment consistently |

Operational semantics for metrics

- Label cardinality: model and region are required; additional labels (customer_id) may be included but cardinality must be capped using the cardinality policy (see related page).
- Aggregation window: RAF uses sliding windows with configurable length (default 5m for short experiments, up to 30m for conservative validation).
- Fidelity: samplers must preserve rare-tail behaviour; use stratified sampling when downsampling traces.

Hypothesis generation and candidate vector format

- Candidate vector is a fixed schema JSON (stored in experiment metadata) with string keys and scalar values. Example keys: kernel_variant, batch_max_tokens, batch_max_items, concurrency_limit, kvcache_policy, quant_profile.

Example candidate vector (YAML for readability):

---
kernel_variant: "fused-attn-v2"
batch_max_tokens: 2048
batch_max_items: 8
concurrency_limit: 12
kvcache_policy: "prefetch-on-hot-prefix"
quant_profile: "int8-mixed"
---

Experiment design and traffic shaping

1) Canary slice (default 0.5% traffic) for 30 minutes.
2) If canary passes acceptance, expand to staged rollout: 1% -> 5% -> 20% with minimum dwell time of 10 minutes per stage.
3) Each stage runs with an active control arm (unchanged parameters) and returns pre/post metrics.

Acceptance criteria (validator rules)

- Latency (tail) regression: 95th percentile tail must not increase by more than +5% relative to control.
- Error budget: error_counts.total must not exceed control by more than +10% absolute or 2x relative (whichever is smaller).
- Cost delta: expected per-token cost must improve or remain within -2% (no >2% cost increase allowed).
- Resource safety: GPU memory usage must not exceed 90% of baseline.
- Guard for degenerate behaviour: if kvcache_hit_ratio drops by >0.05 absolute in canary, abort.

Automated rollback triggers

- Instant rollback on any of the following during a stage:
  - 99.9 latency regressed >10% absolute.
  - OOM errors observed in >0.1% of canary requests.
  - Unhealthy node count increases by >1 per shard.

Experiment telemetry retained for audit

- Every experiment stores: candidate vector, start/end timestamps, aggregated metrics for control and treatment windows (as JSON blobs), decision (approve/reject), operator (automated or user id), git sha for runtime binaries, and rollout graph.
- Retention: 90 days hot, 2 years archived (compliance requirement).

Safety and human-in-the-loop controls

- Any candidate that touches quant_profile or kernel_variant requires an explicit human review for models with customers in restricted compliance tiers.
- Tiered approvals:
  - Low risk: kernel parameter tuning that does not change quant_profile and passes canary -> auto-approve.
  - Medium risk: changes that touch quant_profile but are only conservative adjustments -> require 2 engineering reviewers.
  - High risk: any change that reduces replication or changes memory layout -> product and security review required.

Runbook: how to launch a manual experiment

1) Create a new experiment record in RAF UI or via CLI. Example CLI snippet:

raf experiment create --name "short-seq-batching-optim" --vectors '{"batch_max_tokens":1024,"concurrency_limit":10,"kernel_variant":"fused-attn-v2"}' --canary-percent 0.5 --dwell 30m --owner "team-runtime"

2) Observe RAF dashboard for the canary window (link: /raf/ui/experiments).
3) If validator shows PASS, promote to staged rollout. If FAIL, inspect raw traces and open an incident if necessary.

Troubleshooting checklist (first 60 minutes)

- If canary FAILS:
  1) Check redwood_runtime_autotune_error_counts for error_type=oob/oom/timeout.
  2) Inspect per-shard latency histograms to detect skew.
  3) Compare kvcache_hit_ratio between control and treatment.
  4) If resource saturation is suspected, run ephemeral profiler (profctl snapshot --target shard-X) and capture GPU kernel traces.

- If intermittent tail spikes only during peak traffic, abort staged rollout and reopen with a narrower sequence-length targeted candidate.

Operational responsibilities and ownership

- RAF service owner: eng-serving-runtime team. Primary oncall: runtime-platform-sre.
- Experiment approvers: runtime-performance SIG (listed in team roster).
- Auditing and compliance: security-and-compliance owns retention and access policies for experiment artifacts.

Safety-oriented telemetry sampling policy

- Always keep a separate high-fidelity tail-sampler stream (1 in 100 requests by default) with full traces and raw input signatures (redacted per privacy policy). Do not apply downsampling before safety checks.

Example validation query (Prometheus-like pseudo-query)

"(histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(redwood_runtime_autotune_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le)) )"

Configuration table (defaults and recommended ranges)

- batch_max_tokens: default 1024, allowed range [32, 8192]
- batch_max_items: default 8, allowed range [1, 64]
- concurrency_limit: default 12, allowed range [1, 128]
- quant_profile: default "int8-mixed", allowed values ["fp16", "int8-mixed", "fp32-conservative"]

Release cadence and compatibility

- RAF uses semantic releases aligned with runtime major versions. Each release includes a compatibility matrix: supported kernel variants, required telemetry schema version, and minimum runtime binary git sha. The RAF service rejects experiments that declare an incompatible runtime binary.

Audit and postmortem expectations

- Any automated rollout that triggers a rollback must create an experiment postmortem within 72 hours. The postmortem must include: root cause hypothesis, data artifacts, and corrective action plan (owner and ETA).
